Every log line our Modal apps emit is now one JSON object carrying its real `level`, so severity is queryable in the tier's OpenObserve `modal_logs` stream (`spath(body, 'level')`) even though Modal's OTEL exporter stamps every line `INFO` (mngr-internal#656):

- New `log_format.py`: `JsonLogFormatter` renders each record as `{"timestamp", "level", "logger", "type": "log", "message": ...}`, and `StructuredRecordJsonLogFormatter` (on the dedicated structured-record handlers only) flattens the JSON-object message into the same envelope instead (`http_request` / `metric` / `share_visit_authorized` keep their `type` and fields top-level, so existing consumers such as the analytics log views read them unchanged; a plain log call whose text is a JSON object is never flattened, so it cannot forge a record); `minds_env` is stamped when deployed and tracebacks are folded into one `exception` string.

- New `configure_logging()`: the per-container bootstrap each Modal function calls first (next to `init_sentry`). Previously no root handler existed in the containers at all, so Python dropped every INFO line our packages logged and printed WARNING+ as the bare message; the bootstrap installs one JSON handler on the root logger with third-party libraries held at WARNING and our `imbue.*` packages at INFO, overridable per deploy via `MINDS_LOG_LEVEL`, which the deploy metadata secret now threads into the container when the deployer exports it.

- `capture_and_reraise` (the cron / spawned-function wrapper) now also logs the escaping exception as one `level: ERROR` record with the folded traceback before re-raising, so a failed cron is severity-queryable in the log store rather than visible only as Modal's level-less raw traceback lines; the SDK's Dedupe integration keeps Bugsink at one event.

- `ensure_info_log_handler` (the access-log / metric / share-visit loggers) installs the structured-record JSON formatter; the old `%(asctime)s` text prefix is gone. `deployed_minds_env_name` moved to `log_format.py` (still importable from `request_logging`'s callers via the new module).
